boundary: Repository-scoped autonomous coding agent on GitHub; it produces branch/commit/PR artifacts, not a general no-code application runtime.
workflows: Researches a repository, plans, edits on a branch, runs tests/linters, iterates, and opens a pull request; automations can trigger scheduled or event-driven work.
prompting_planning: Natural-language task prompts, repository context, implementation plans, follow-up steering, custom agents and issue/PR entry points are documented.
generated_artifacts: Branch commits, diffs, tests/linters, session logs and pull requests; generated app schema, visual design model and deterministic build manifest are unknown.
data_auth_integration: Repository context and configurable MCP/server/tool access are documented; credential scopes, external SaaS data policy and production auth/data migration are unknown.
ui_design: Can change UI code and improve tests, but no first-party claim establishes visual design generation or accessibility guarantees.
runtime_sandbox: Ephemeral GitHub Actions development environment, automated tests and restricted internet/firewall are documented; complete resource limits and tenant isolation details are unknown.
deploy_export: GitHub branch/commit/PR handoff is strong; deployment/export is through the repository ecosystem, not a documented hosted app publish or infrastructure export contract.
collaboration: Issues, PRs, reviewers, Teams/Slack integrations, co-authored commits, signed commits and auditable logs provide strong collaboration traceability.
recovery: Branch/diff/commit history and PR iteration support code recovery; database restore, external side-effect reversal and replay are unknown.
governance_security: Write-access gating, branch protections, human merge approval, secret scanning, CodeQL/advisory checks, firewall and admin audit logs are documented; retention and full tenant controls are unknown.
economics: Available on paid Copilot plans; cloud-agent usage costs and current plan entitlements are time-sensitive and not normalized here.
contradictions: The product is an engineering agent with strong repository governance, not evidence of a general application-builder surface.
